title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', his study of the action of Gal(Q̄/Q), or of an abstract automorphism u, on the profinite fundamental group π̂_{0,3} of P^1 − {0,1,∞}. Here π̂_{0,3} is the profinite free group on the lassos ℓ_0, ℓ_1, with ℓ_∞ determined by ℓ_0ℓ_1ℓ_∞ = 1. The cyclic automorphism ρ (0→1→∞) and the involution τ come from the S_3-symmetry. The automorphism u is described by:
- a multiplier ρ = χ(u) = 2σ+1 ∈ Ẑ*, the cyclotomic character value;
- a 'twisting' element g (equivalently g_0, h_0, ξ).
The 'loop equation' (**) (cf. (68)) is the profinite analogue of the Drinfeld–Ihara relations defining elements (λ, f) of GT^, with ρ playing the role of λ and m = σ = (ρ−1)/2. ξ is put in a 'primitive form' ξ = λ ρ(λ)^{-1} or ξ = λ h_0^{-1} ρ(λ)^{-1}, with λ ∈ π̂_{0,3}·(1,τ).

The step on this page. Map π̂_{0,3} to its congruence image π(2)' = Ker(SL(2,Ẑ)' → SL(2,Z/2)), using the classical identification of π_{0,3} with Γ(2) via ℓ_0 ↦ (1 2; 0 1) and ℓ_1 ↦ (1 0; 2 1). There the loop equation becomes almost trivial: it says ρD = 1, where D = δ(c^2+cd+d^2) and δ = ±1. Here (a b; c d) is the image of λ, and δ is fixed by the residue class mod 3 (ρ ≡ ±1 mod 3, from the previous page). The form c^2+cd+d^2 is the norm form of the Eisenstein integers Z[ω], reflecting the order-3 rotation ρ.

Consequences drawn on the page:
- For fixed ρ the condition is just D ∈ Ẑ* (103).
- Conversely ξ determines λ, hence c, d and δ, hence D, hence the multiplier ρ = 1/D. So ξ alone recovers the whole datum: σ = (ρ−1)/2, then h_0 = ℓ_0^{-σ}ξ, then g_0 via g_0^{-1}τ_∞(g_0) = h_0 (66), then g = τ_∞(g_0) ℓ_1^σ ρ(g_0)^{-1} (62), then the automorphism u via (50). This is the analogue of the statement that in GT^ the component λ is determined by f.
- Consistency check: under the ambiguity (69), ξ ↦ ℓ_0^{-α} ξ ℓ_1^α, the lower-right entry D of the image matrix is unchanged, by the explicit product (104). So the recovered multiplier is well defined.
- Remark 2 warns that the image of ξ in the congruence group SL(2,Ẑ)' gives ρ only up to sign. The image of λ in GL(2,Ẑ)', a matrix of SL(2,Z) defined up to sign, gives ρ exactly as 1/D (continued on the next page).
- The next page checks, prime by prime, that every unit of Ẑ* is of the form ±(norm form) with c even and d odd. This is consistent with surjectivity of the cyclotomic character.
errors: Sign convention in (104): with ℓ_0 ↦ (1 2; 0 1) one should have ℓ_0^{-α} ↦ (1 −2α; 0 1), not (1 2α; 0 1). Grothendieck's matrices correspond to ℓ_0^{α} (or to the opposite generator convention). The multiplication itself is correct for the matrices written, and the conclusion (D invariant) holds either way.

Notational overload: ρ denotes both the cyclic automorphism of π̂_{0,3} (in λρ(λ)^{-1}, ρ(g_0)) and the multiplier χ(u) ∈ Ẑ*. This makes 'donc ρ par (50)' ambiguous; it most likely means the automorphism u.
The determination of ρ 'from ξ' passes through λ, which the page says is uniquely determined by ξ. This uniqueness is asserted (the primitive-form decomposition (94)) and not re-proved here.

ideas.what: Reduction of the loop (hexagon-type) equation to the congruence quotient Γ(2)^ ⊂ SL(2,Ẑ). There it becomes the norm condition ρ·δ(c^2+cd+d^2) = 1 for the Eisenstein norm form.
ideas.modern_name: Image of GT^ / Gal(Q̄/Q) in the congruence completion of Γ(2); the cyclotomic character read off from the modular (SL_2) quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related ideas appear in Ihara's work on Galois representations on π_1 of P^1−{0,1,∞} and in Lochak–Schneps / Nakamura on GT and SL_2 quotients (unsure of the exact statement)

ideas.what: The 'f' part ξ of the automorphism determines the multiplier ρ = χ(u), hence σ = m, and the whole automorphism.
ideas.modern_name: λ is determined by f for (λ,f) ∈ GT^

ideas.what: The congruence image of ξ gives the multiplier only up to sign; the image of λ in GL(2) up to sign gives it exactly via 1/D.
ideas.modern_name: Sign ambiguity of the cyclotomic character in the SL_2-quotient

ideas.what: Invariance of D under the conjugation ambiguity ξ ↦ ℓ_0^{-α}ξℓ_1^α, checked by explicit 2×2 matrix computation.

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly relates the multiplier (cyclotomic character) of a solution of the loop equation to the Eisenstein norm form c^2+cd+d^2 of the bottom row of the congruence image of λ. He thereby reads χ(u) off a quadratic-form value attached to the order-3 symmetry. This explicit modular/norm-form reading of the GT-type equation is a small but concrete computation not standard in the GT literature as far as I know.
missed.quote: on détermine alors ρ de façon unique en termes de D, donc de c et de d et du signe δ par D=δ(c^2+d^2+cd) (a et b sont inutiles)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an elementary description of the image of GT^ or Gal(Q̄/Q) in the congruence quotient of Γ(2)^. This could be useful for questions about the 'modular' or congruence shadow of GT^, though the content is likely recoverable by specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful and correct worked computation inside Grothendieck's private GT-type analysis. The explicit norm-form expression of the multiplier in the congruence quotient is a nice detail, but it is elementary and likely implicit in later work (Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps).
transcription_corrections: The letter transcribed 'p' (e.g. 'on détermine alors p', 'le multiplicateur p = 2σ+1', 'déterminer le multiplicateur p') is Grothendieck's ρ (rho), the multiplier χ(u), consistent with the previous page.
'donc ρ par (50)' likely reads 'donc u par (50)': the automorphism u is recovered at the end of the chain.
The struck-out insertion near the start ('ξ∈Π̂_{0,3}' over an erased word) is a correction above 'de façon unique'.
Margin 'NB On a [...] ρ' — the margin note concerns ρ; it is mostly illegible.
